hypothesis: An EEG estimate of how a photo differs from the other photos of its object in specific regions can supply spatial conditions to diffusion while retaining the established global word and H/14 direction.
subject: sub-04, four physical EEG trials per picture
development: Sample 128 training objects from the original 416, and 32 development objects from the historical 96. Draw without replacement in that order with NumPy default_rng(260558), sort each selection. Use all ten photos per object. These are previously studied generic objects. No personal12 photo is included.
features: Center crop each archived stimulus to 512 square as in the generator evaluation. Four overlapping 352 by 352 windows have top-left offsets (0,0), (160,0), (0,160), (160,160), in (x,y) order. Resize each to 224 square with bicubic resampling, encode with the pinned LAION ViT-H/14, unit-normalize each projected vector. Subtract the mean of the four regional vectors within each photograph to remove its common visual content.
readout: Use the native posterior 1003 features. Fit a single within-object ridge with fixed penalty twice the sample count, historical per-coordinate EEG standardization, and four concatenated 1024-dimensional regional contrasts. Each held-out pair shares the other eight photos as calibration. Predicted spatial change is query output minus mean support output. Primary statistic is the within-photo sum of squared regional-feature error, averaged over ten photos per object. Compare to zero residual and a control that rotates the predicted four regions through 180 degrees. Also report paired photo assignment, and exchanged EEG as a direction check.
image_gate: If the mean squared regional error improves over zero and over the rotated field with positive lower 95% object-bootstrap bounds, compare actual sub-04 personal12 reconstructions. This panel's earlier output scores are known. Preserve its mixed-readout word, global H/14, original noise, and four steps. Use four masked images within one base H/14 IP-Adapter, one per quadrant. Each direction starts at the frozen global H/14 direction, adds half the predicted local contrast field, then renormalizes. A field contains the eight-support mean regional contrast plus the photo residual. Compare support prior, matched, exchanged within-word/fold fields, and flat copies of the global condition. Score the independent saved images against the original, especially DINO within-object photo retrieval and unchanged object naming. No oracle as an inference input.
